subject: Skyline: pricing simulation request — burst credits & elastic tiers
messages:
From: Elena Diaz <elena.diaz@skyline.ai>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API pricing + burst/elastic tiers (high throughput)

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. Skyline is running an internal evaluation for a new personalization pipeline that will be heavy on hosted inference — we're estimating baseline usage around 120M tokens/day (roughly 3.6B tokens/month) with the following profile:

- Baseline steady state: ~4–5 reqs/s sustained (mostly short prompts)
- Periodic spikes: short windows (minutes–hours) where traffic multiplies ~8–12x (marketing launches, Black Friday-like events twice a year)
- Seasonal surges: ~2 months/year with sustained 3x baseline for longer windows

We need a pricing proposal that covers:
1) Baseline unit pricing for hosted API (prompt vs completion if you differentiate)
2) An elastic / burst credit policy — how many tokens of burst before overage, whether credits carry over, and how quickly you can scale up during spikes
3) How discounts are applied as volume increases (is it blended, step-down tiers, or committed buckets?)
4) Any options to cap spend or apply surge caps to avoid runaway bills

Can you run three modeled scenarios and send back an example monthly bill for each?
A. Steady monthly (3.6B tokens)
B. Spiky monthly (same total tokens but concentrated into spikes)
C. Seasonal (two months at 3x baseline)

If helpful, cc'ing billing. We need a formal quote by next Tuesday (2026-12-08) so procurement can review.

Thanks — Elena

Elena Diaz
Head of Platform Engineering, Skyline Commerce

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing + burst/elastic tiers (high throughput)

Elena — thanks for the clear traffic profile, that helps a lot. I ran a quick pass and attached two artifacts: a PDF overview of our elastic tiering approach and a baseline simulation workbook (attached) with three scenarios modeled. High level notes below; Ben is on copy and will finalize numbers + a formal quote.

Summary (short):
- Baseline hosted unit price (public hosted catalog reference): generation: $0.00045 per token; context/prompt: $0.00012 per token.
- Elastic tiers: we apply a blended step-down for sustained monthly consumption and a separate short-term burst credit pool that lets you exceed baseline throughput without immediate overage for short windows.
- Burst credit policy (recommended for Skyline): 10% of committed monthly tokens available as immediate burst capacity, replenished daily up to cap; additional burst is billed at a short-term overage rate with threshold-based throttles available to protect spend.

Proposed approach for Skyline (we can tweak):
- Commit model: you pick a committed monthly baseline (e.g., 3.6B tokens). Discounts apply on the incremental usage above thresholds in a step-down fashion (see attached for breakpoints).
- Burst buffer: 10% unlocked automatically; you can request temporary expansion to 50% for planned events (one-time 30-day allowance) at a reduced ramp fee.
- Carryover: unused committed tokens can carry forward up to 15% for one billing period if you opt-in.

I'll let Ben share the modeled dollar outputs and an alternate option with a short-term reserved slab for predictable latency (Dedicated capacity) if you care about P99 latency guarantees.

Next steps:
- Ben to send three scenario quotes and a formal quote/MAA PDF by 2026-12-07 EOD
- If Skyline wants a limited-time 30-day increased burst to cover the upcoming product campaign, flag that in your reply and we can provision it.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 14:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Skyline — simulated billing scenarios + burst policy options (attachment)

Elena / Grace,

Attached is the simulation workbook (burst_simulation_skyline.xlsx) and a compact quote table. Highlights pulled from the workbook:

Scenario A — Steady 3.6B tokens/month
- Modeled as blended step-tier (no spikes)
- Effective blended rate: $0.00032/token
- Estimated monthly bill: $1,152,000

Scenario B — Spiky (same total tokens but concentrated)
- Uses burst buffer for minute-to-hour spikes; we simulated 12x short peaks across 20 events/month
- Burst buffer covered ~72% of peak minutes; remainder billed at overage short-term rate ($0.00048/token)
- Estimated monthly bill: $1,198,400 (includes 30-day temporary ramp fee of $8,000)

Scenario C — Seasonal (two months at 3x baseline)
- For months with sustained 3x, blended rate steps down after month 1; we simulated opting into temporary expanded burst (50%) for the two months
- Estimated average monthly bill across quarter: $1,880,000 (seasonal months higher, off months lower due to carryover)

Burst credit mechanics we used in the simulation:
- Auto-burst pool = 10% of committed monthly tokens (replenished daily up to cap)
- Temporary expansion = up to 50% for a one-time 30-day window (requires 7-day notice for pre-provisioning; discounted ramp fee applies)
- Carryover = up to 15% of unused committed tokens for next billing cycle (opt-in)

Attachments:
- burst_simulation_skyline.xlsx (scenario tabs, assumptions, raw token traces)
- redwood_flex_tiers_v1.pdf (explanatory appendix and sample contract language)

A few asks for accuracy:
1) Can you confirm the expected ratio of prompt:length to completion:length? (we assumed 1:2 for this sim)
2) Any strict budget caps you want us to enforce (we can set hard spend ceilings per day/week)?
3) Do you want Dedicated capacity pricing alongside hosted? I included a placeholder model — we can formalize if you prefer latency SLAs.

If these numbers look directionally correct, I can generate a formal quote and MSA addendum for Skyline.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0110

- We'd like a formal quote that includes: (a) hosted blended pricing (with step-down detail), (b) an option for a 30-day 50% burst pre-provision at reduced ramp fee, and (c) a parallel Dedicated capacity quote with P99 latency targets + monthly commit comparison.
- Procurement requests: can you include a clause that allows converting unused committed tokens into a credit towards Dedicated onboarding fees? That would make our tax/proc teams happier.

Also — we plan a marketing campaign starting 2027-01-18 that will likely require the temporary expansion. Please hold the 30-day temporary expansion for Skyline and send the formal quote/MAA by EOD 2026-12-08 so procurement can sign and we can schedule provisioning.

I'll loop in our procurement lead once we have the formal docs.

Best,
Elena
